title: Laptop Stand
description: I designed and 3D-printed a custom laptop stand in Fusion 360 to improve ventilation during gaming, applying parametric modeling and 3D-printing techniques.

timeline.heading: Objective
timeline.description: For this project, I wanted to create a stand to place my laptop on to allow for better ventilation on the bottom of the laptop when I'm gaming. To do this, I decided to model it in Fusion and 3D print it to gain better experience with those skillsets.

timeline.heading: Modeling
timeline.description: I wanted to learn how to add parameters into my project so I can easily tweak individual values. I had some experience coming into this project, as I 3D modeled a Lego Brick and a box in my Engineering class, but I hadn't applied those skills to a larger project like this. Initially, I was overwhelmed since I didn't know where to start. Soon, I realized that instead of worrying about the whole project, I needed to start small and expand from there. I thought modeling a leg was a good place to start. Then, I mirrored the leg to the other side and connect the legs at multiple points to ensure stability. Throughout the project, I used parameters to control the dimensions of the sketches and extrusions, which could easily be tweaked in the parameters page in Fusion.

timeline.heading: 3D Printing
timeline.description: I imported the model into Orcaslicer to customize the print settings. I kept the default print settings for my printer and PLA, but I added supports over the parts of the stand that overhang so the overhand will print properly.

timeline.heading: Final Product
timeline.description: Overall, I think this project turned out well as my laptop fits on the stand and has proper ventilation underneath it. I also learned more about Fusion and 3D modeling, both from a technical standpoint, as well as a mental standpoint. However, there are a few things I could've done better. First, while the support did well at supporting the overhang during printing, it was difficult to remove. I wasn't able to remove some of the support from the final product. I think using tree supports will help address this issue. Also, while I was using the stand, I realized I couldn't route wires underneath the stand as the front bar block it, which was a problem when I was using my keyboard in front of it. I could fix it by atleast creating a gap for wires to go through. Lastly, I could make the stand better by optimizing the thickness of the stand to be as thin as possible and giving the stand the ability to adjust size and fold. I plan to address these issues in future iterations of the stand.
